title: Observation of correlation-driven topological transport and robust ferromagnetism in 2D CrS$_2$
authors: Sk Md Obaidulla, M. Nur Hasan, Dayal Das, Rafiqul Alam, Antonio Supina, Muhammad Awais Aslam, Sherif Kamal, Iva Šarić Jankovic, Aleksandar Matkovic, Christian Teichert, Atindra Nath Pal, Heike C. Herper, Marko Kralj
abstract: The realization of correlated layered magnets hosting robust ferromagnetism with emergent topological transport remains a key challenge in quantum materials. Here we report the first catalyst-free chemical vapour deposition growth of layered 1T-CrS$_2$, establishing a highly stable vdWs ferromagnet with an out-of-plane easy-axis anisotropy and a Curie temperature above room temperature. Transport measurements reveal a semimetal--insulator crossover near 80 K and pronounced negative magnetoresistance up to 350 K. A topological Hall effect emerges below 30 K, a rare signature of correlated transport in layered transition-metal dichalcogenide ferromagnets. First-principles calculations show that spin--orbit coupling gaps Dirac-like crossings, while electronic correlations reconstruct the Fermi surface by suppressing electron pockets and reducing the carrier density, enhancing momentum-dependent out-of-plane spin polarization. Magnetic measurements, supported by Heisenberg exchange calculations, reveal strong nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic exchange that stabilizes long-range ferromagnetism. Our results establish 1T-CrS$_2$ as a rare correlated 3$d$ layered ferromagnet in which electronic correlations and spin--orbit coupling cooperatively drive emergent topological transport.
summary: This work reports the synthesis and characterization of $1T-	ext{CrS}_2$, demonstrating it as a promising layered magnet. The research combines experimental transport measurements showing topological effects with sophisticated theoretical calculations that prove these phenomena arise from the cooperative action of electronic correlations and spin-orbit coupling in this correlated material.
main_problem: The challenge is realizing a single 2D platform that robustly integrates correlated magnetism, electronic topology, and transport phenomena in layered magnets.
main_result: The study establishes $1T-	ext{CrS}_2$ as a rare correlated 3d layered ferromagnet where electronic correlations and spin-orbit coupling cooperatively drive emergent topological transport.
method: A combination of experimental techniques (CVD growth, transport/magnetization measurements) and advanced theoretical calculations ($	ext{DFT}+U+	ext{SOC}$, Heisenberg exchange) was employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is layered $1T-	ext{CrS}_2$, a transition-metal dichalcogenide known for its octahedral coordination, which promotes strong electron correlations and intrinsic magnetism.
key_observables: Robust ferromagnetism with out-of-plane easy-axis anisotropy; semimetal–insulator crossover near 80 K; topological Hall effect below 30 K; gap opening upon inclusion of SOC/correlations.
important_parameters: Curie temperature ($T_C$) above room temperature; low temperatures ($	ext{T} < 30	ext{ K}$) for topological effects; correlation strength ($U$).
main_assumptions: The study assumes the stability and synthesizability of the $1T$ polymorph via CVD, and uses theoretical models (like $\Delta_\alpha(T)$) to describe temperature-dependent crossovers.
figures_summary: Figures show crystal structures, temperature dependence of resistance revealing a crossover, calculated spectral functions comparing DFT vs. SOC vs. correlated methods, and 2D Fermi surface projections under different theoretical treatments.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reporting the synthesis (CVD) and basic magnetic/transport measurements. It then uses advanced electronic structure calculations ($	ext{DFT} 	o 	ext{DFT}+	ext{SOC} 	o 	ext{DFT}+U+	ext{SOC}$) to explain the observed phenomena, culminating in a unified picture of correlation-driven topological transport.
why_interesting: The interplay between strong electron correlations (Hubbard physics), spin-orbit coupling, and emergent topology is central to modern condensed matter theory, making this highly relevant for understanding correlated materials beyond simple band theory.

Fig. 3e shows the calculated isotropic exchange parameters Jij as a function of the normalized Cr–Cr distance (Rij/a). The calculated exchange interactions are predominantly ferromagnetic and remain finite over several neighbouring shells. Interestingly, although the nearest-neighbour exchange interaction is ferromagnetic, the second- and third-nearest-neighbour couplings become comparatively stronger. This behaviour reflects the itinerant nature of magnetic exchange in 1T- CrS2, where indirect Cr–S–Cr hybridization enhances intermediate-range exchange pathways beyond the shortest Cr–Cr distance.
